correctness.rationale: For n>=3 the weighted matrix-tree identity gives the full unnormalized signed spanning-tree Walsh coefficient as the determinant of M(r,s) with the precise signed (not absolute-degree) reduced Laplacian. Unsigned wheel trees are L_(2n)-2 and have odd count for 3∤n, forcing every signed coefficient odd. For n=3k and arbitrary 2k signs u_j,t_j, the exact (1,1,2)-periodic vector annihilates the specified signed M and yields 4^k distinct zeros. For n divisible by 3, all edge inclusion counts are even: spoke count F_(2n), rim count tau-F_(2n), and total tau=L_(2n)-2 is 0 mod4 by the Lucas matrix recurrence; each signed coefficient is tau-2 sum_{negative e}N_e mod4, so universally divisible by four. Independently checked all 4/16 period-three witnesses at n=3,6 by exact integer matrix multiplication, and small n wheel tree counts; the general proof is algebraic, not inferred from examples.
residual_risks: The explicit 4^(n/3) zero lower bound is not asserted sharp; exact zero counts for large n remain unknown.
